add.issue.name: The SEA GUI asset check skips Windows — nobody has run it on a Windows runner

edit.description.md:
`build-sea.mjs` step 7 boots `epiq gui` from the freshly built binary and pulls every asset `index.html` references, so `sea.getAsset` is exercised (added for `DSBC69B`). It is skipped on `win32`.

Why it was skipped rather than shipped untested: the release matrix builds `epiq-windows-x64.exe` on `windows-latest`, and a new runtime step there that nobody could try first risks breaking a release build. Two Windows-specific hazards were identified and not resolved:

- `openBrowser` spawns `cmd /c start "" <url>` there, where the posix `open`/`xdg-open` PATH shim does not apply.
- `rmSync` on the child's own cwd right after `kill` can hit EBUSY on Windows. Cleanup is already best-effort, so this one is probably handled.

What the skip does *not* cost: the asset map is built identically on every platform, so a missing or misnamed asset is caught on the macOS and Linux legs regardless. The gap is Windows-specific *runtime* behaviour of the packaged GUI only.

To close: run `npm run build:binary` on a Windows runner with the skip removed and see whether it serves.

add.issue.name: The scrubber's "Now" label claims the timeline's far end is the present, even over a past window

edit.description.md:
The status label at the right of the scrubber controls (`ScrubberParts.tsx`, the Resume/Now button) reads "Now" whenever the board is live. It sits directly above the right end of the track, so it reads as naming that end — and once the window is a past one, whether paged back with the period arrows or dragged out as a zoom, that end is not the present and the label is a lie.

Show it only while the window actually runs up to the present. That is the `atLatest` flag the pager already uses to decide whether there is anywhere later to page to.

"Resume" is unaffected: it is an action rather than a claim about the far end, and stays wherever the board is parked. The slot keeps its width either way so the row does not shift.

- **Linux arm64** (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`): `npm run build:binary` inside the `epiq-e2e` container (`node:22-bookworm`, no browser, no `xdg-open`, no epiq config, fresh `EPIQ_GLOBAL_DIR`) — same result. This was the leg worth proving: the check boots a server and needs no display.

- **Windows** (`windows-latest`): deliberately skipped — see `Y7RKPTH`.

Also hardened while there: temp-directory cleanup is best-effort, so a directory the build cannot remove logs rather than failing a release.

add.issue.comment.md:
The first real CI run (PR 170) failed, and it was worth it — the new job found two more things nothing else could.

**1. Ink goes quiet in CI.** Every `waitFor` in `seed-tui.ts` timed out on *empty* output: `Timed out waiting for "choose your username". Last 1200 chars:` followed by nothing. Ink stops rendering frame by frame when it detects CI and writes only the final frame on unmount, so the pty stays silent. `source/test/e2e/e2e.helper.ts` already `delete`s `CI` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS` for exactly this reason; the GUI seeder never got it, because it had never run anywhere with `CI` set. Fixed the same way.

Worth noting the container rehearsal could not have caught this: Docker does not set `CI`, so `epiq-e2e` looked green.

**2. The QA board was seeded by luck.** Chasing the failure surfaced this in `seedProject`:

```
tui.input(':new board QA');
await tui.waitFor('<ENTER> to confirm');
tui.input('\r');
await tui.waitFor('QA');   // already true — the typed command is on screen
```

The command being typed is itself rendered, so `QA` is in the buffer before ENTER is sent. That wait returned immediately and `destroy()` could land before the board was written, leaving a seeded repo whose switcher has nothing to switch to. It usually won the race; under load it did not — the two tests that failed in one local run were precisely the two that need the QA board. Added `forget()` and cleared the buffer before the wait, so it can only be satisfied by a frame drawn after ENTER. Verified `QA` does redraw then, so the wait is now real rather than merely longer.

Also set `IS_CI=true` in `test:gui:ci`, matching `test:e2e:ci`: `playwright.config.ts` already keys `forbidOnly` and the reporter off it, so without it a stray `test.only` would have sailed through CI.

add.issue.name: Name an agent with a CLI argument, not just EPIQ_USER_NAME

edit.description.md:
`EPIQ_USER_NAME` is the only way to give a process its own board identity, which forces an `env` block into every MCP client config.

Add an argument form that writes into the same resolution path:

- `epiq-mcp <name>` — positional, since `source/mcp/index.ts` ignores argv today.
- `epiq --as <name>` / `epiq gui --as <name>` — a flag, because the `epiq` binary already spends `input[0]` on the command slot (`gui`).

Both set `process.env[EPIQ_USER_NAME]` before boot, so `resolveEnvActor` and the config-edit guard in `commands.ts` keep working through one path. An argument and a conflicting env var is an error, not a silent precedence rule. Error text must name whichever source supplied the bad value.

Rejected: renaming the var to `NAME`. Env vars are one inherited namespace and `NAME` is widely set already (shell loop variable, adduser, CI images). Because `deriveActorId` makes a name a permanent contributor id and `tombstoneContributor` refuses authors, a stray inherited `NAME` would be an unremovable bogus contributor. The `EPIQ_` prefix is what makes the var safe to trust.

`EPIQ_USER_ID` stays env-only.

add.issue.comment.md:
Second CI run got much further — seeding worked, 64 of 65 passed. The one failure was `offline.pw.ts`, and it is a real race rather than load:

The test cuts the socket and asserts the `reconnecting` pill. With the retry schedule scaled to 0.2 the first attempt is scheduled 100ms after the cut and succeeds immediately against a local server, so the state exists for about a tenth of a second — not a window a poll can be relied on to land in. It holds on a 14-core laptop and misses on a 4-vCPU runner.

Fixed by holding the state still instead of racing it: refuse the retries while the assertions run, then allow them and assert it recovers on its own. Dropped the init-script scaling for that phase (so refusing leaves ~15s of headroom before the attempts are spent) and set the 0.2 scale via `page.evaluate` just before the phase that actually needs a short schedule.

Second change, aimed at the same class of failure: `workers` was hardcoded to 6. A worker seeds by driving a real TUI through a pty and then holds two servers and a browser; six of those want more than the four vCPUs a hosted runner has. Now `process.env['IS_CI'] ? 2 : 6`.

Committed on the branch but **not pushed** — the machine is at load 100+ with other agents running, so neither the local gate nor a measurement of the flake rate means anything right now. Baseline before the change was 3 clean full runs then one flake (`scatter-gesture`) as load climbed past 85.

Open question for whoever picks this up: whether the gate should also get `retries` in CI. It would make the job reliable immediately, but it hides exactly the kind of race found above, so it is a deliberate trade rather than an obvious fix.

`applyActorNameArgument` treats the argument and the variable as agreeing when they normalize alike, then writes the argument's casing into the environment. With `EPIQ_USER_ID` pinned, `resolveEnvActor` returns the name unnormalized, so the display name follows whichever casing the argument used.

add.issue.name: GUI preferences vanish when the server falls back to a random port

edit.description.md:
`listen` in `source/gui/api/api-server.ts:163-199` prefers 3710 and, on EADDRINUSE, retries with `tryListen(0)` — an **ephemeral** port, different on every run. Since web storage is scoped to the whole origin (scheme + host + **port**), every instance that loses 3710 gets its own storage, and gets a *new* one each time it starts. So the second GUI on a machine effectively has amnesia: panel width, board selection, scrubber flags and any lane-collapse state all reset every launch.

Switching to IndexedDB would not help — localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and the Cache API are all origin-scoped the same way. Cookies are the one exception (scoped by host and path, ignoring port), but they are a poor fit: sent on every request, ~4KB, and visible to the server.

Two real options:

**A. Deterministic port fallback** — 3710, then 3711, 3712… instead of `0`. Cheap, and each instance keeps stable storage across runs. Does not help someone who opens the same board from two different ports.

**B. Move GUI preferences server-side** — epiq already has a config layer and an open websocket, so prefs could live with the project/global config instead of the browser. Fixes it for every instance and every browser, and is the only option that makes prefs follow the *project* rather than the origin. Bigger change, and it needs a decision on scope: per-project or global, and whether prefs sync between machines like board state does.

Current keys affected: `epiq.aside.width`, `epiq.board.selection`, the scrubber `usePersistedFlag` keys, and any lane-collapse key added by RVZSAKH.

Raised by the user while reviewing RVZSAKH. Not blocking it — that ticket uses localStorage to match the existing keys, and they should all move together if B is chosen.

add.issue.name: A bulk tag intermittently reaches only one of the selected tickets

edit.description.md:
`bulk.pw.ts:26` ("picking several tickets opens a bulk overview") fails intermittently on the assertion that both tickets carry the bulk-applied tag:

```
Locator: div[draggable="true"] >> hasText 'B873121-' >> hasText 'bulky'
Expected: 2   Received: 1
  3 × locator resolved to 0 elements
  60 × locator resolved to 1 element
```

Sixty polls stuck at one, so the second ticket is genuinely untagged rather than slow to render. The tag is applied while both are selected, and the panel does show it.

**What is known**

- Reproduces only inside a full-suite run (roughly one run in five). 24 consecutive runs of `bulk.pw.ts` on its own all passed.
- Ruled out: the client fires one request per picked ticket concurrently (`forPicked(id => addIssueTag(id, name))` in `App.tsx`), but both GUI transports wrap mutations in `runExclusive` (`api-server.ts`, `lib/websocket.ts`), so the writes are serialised server-side.
- Ruled out: `nodeRepo.createTag` has no duplicate-name guard, so a lost `create.tag` for a name that already exists is not the mechanism.
- Not yet established: whether the second `add.issue.tag` is never sent, or is sent and lost. Note `addIssueTag` updates GUI state optimistically and then fire-and-forgets over the socket, and the test's `expect(aside).toContainText('bulky')` is satisfied by that optimistic state — so the test navigates away without knowing the server has both writes. That makes the test unsound regardless of whether it is the cause here.

Predates the CI work; found while getting the GUI suite green in CI for `9710XT1`, which is where it started costing something — it is now the one thing keeping that gate from being reliable.

Worth reading the epiq-architecture notes before touching the event side.

add.issue.comment.md:
**Option C, from the user: detect the occupied port at boot and offer to claim it.**

This is better than A or B, because it attacks the cause (an unstable origin) rather than the symptom. But "free the port" should be the last step of C, not the first — the common occupant of 3710 is *another epiq GUI*, and killing it is the wrong answer to most of the cases:

- **Occupant is epiq on the same project.** Don't start a second server at all: open the browser at the one already running. Same origin, prefs intact, nothing killed, and it fixes the duplicate-board confusion too. This is the case that actually happens most, and it needs no prompt.
- **Occupant is epiq on a different project.** Killing it yanks the rug from another board someone is reading. Prompt, and offer both: take the port, or carry on with a fallback (accepting separate prefs).
- **Occupant is not epiq.** Somebody else's dev server on 3710. The most dangerous case, and the only one where "free the port" means killing a stranger's process. Explicit prompt, never a default.

**What is missing to do this safely:** the server knows `project.repoRoot` (`api-server.ts:215`) but exposes no identity. A `GET /api/instance` returning `{app: 'epiq', repoRoot, version, pid}` makes "who holds 3710?" answerable by probing the port, rather than inferred from `lsof` and a guess. That endpoint is the enabler for all three branches above and is small on its own.

**Costs of the kill path specifically**, worth weighing before committing to it:
- Windows is a shipped target (`epiq-windows-x64.exe` in ci.yml), so freeing a port needs `lsof -ti` on macOS/Linux *and* `netstat -ano` + `taskkill` on Windows.
- Killing by port is racy: the holder can change between the lookup and the signal.
- A prompt cannot block a non-interactive start (CI, `--headless`, the e2e suites), so it needs a flag and a documented default.

**Suggested split**, since the first part is non-destructive and useful alone:
1. Add the instance endpoint, and reuse a same-project server instead of starting a second one. Removes most occurrences of the whole problem without touching storage or killing anything.
2. Only then decide whether the remaining cases get a reclaim prompt (C) or a deterministic fallback (A).

Option B (prefs server-side) stays worth doing independently — it is the only one that makes prefs follow the project across browsers and machines — but it is no longer urgent if 1 lands.

`GET /api/instance` returns `{app, repoRoot, version, pid}` and is answered before the board is read, so a probe costs a socket. `startGui` probes `PREFERRED_GUI_PORT` before starting anything; a same-project answer means it opens the browser at that server and returns, never calling `startGuiServer`.

- `startGuiServer` is untouched, which is what keeps the e2e suites (they call it directly) on isolated ports.

add.issue.name: epiq skill: attach a screenshot only in special cases, cropped and compressed

edit.description.md:
BP59K8E added "Show the result when it is visual" to `.claude/skills/epiq/SKILL.md`, which reads as a default: attach a screenshot whenever the work changed something you can see. Two corrections wanted.

**Special case, not default.** Most outcomes are better described than photographed. An image should earn its place — a layout that has to be seen, a rendering bug, a chart — rather than being routine in a `Solution:` comment.

**Crop and compress before attaching.** The skill says nothing about size, and the facts make that expensive:

- `epiq_issue_attachment_add` stores the file as it finds it. Only the GUI compresses on upload (`compress-image.ts` is client-only), so an agent's raw screenshot goes in untouched, up to the 500 KB cap.
- The blob lands in `.epiq/media/` on the state branch, which replicates to every clone.
- It is never removed: deleting an attachment writes a tombstone and the bytes stay, so time travel can still resolve them. `media-store.ts` has no unlink.

So an oversized screenshot is permanent, for everybody — the same argument the text limits are built on.

edit.description.md:

Size is not the lever — 12 is the project's de facto standard (17 of 22 icon usages; the rest are 13 or 14 for specific spots), so inflating this one would make it the odd control in the panel.

Drop the centre bar: `><` to collapse and `<>` to expand, leaving a 6-unit gap between the chevron tips (3px at render). Same convention, half the marks to resolve.

`bulk.pw.ts:26` intermittently failed the assertion that both tickets carry the bulk-applied tag — `Expected: 2 Received: 1`, with sixty polls stuck at one, so the second ticket was genuinely untagged rather than slow to render.

**Investigated and not reproducible. The product path is sound.**

Driving the real GUI websocket exactly as the client does — two `issue:tag:add` messages for a brand-new tag name, sent in the same tick, one per selected ticket — then reading the server's own state back:

- 20/20 rounds, both tickets tagged, no failed results, no duplicate tag nodes.
- 20/20 again with the repo's index left dirty, the way a failed `commitLinkedFile` left it (`git add` succeeded, `git commit` did not).

Also ruled out by reading: `issue:tag:add` **is** in `MUTATING_MESSAGE_TYPES`, so both GUI transports serialise it through `runExclusive`; `pickedIssues` and the panel's "N tickets selected" come from the same list, so a fan-out over a shorter list would have shown a smaller count; and `SwimlaneColumn` has no per-lane render cap that could hide a card.

The symptom has not recurred in **12 consecutive full-suite runs** since the unrelated commit-path collision was fixed under `9710XT1`, against roughly three failures in thirteen runs before it. No mechanism links the two, so this is correlation, not a proven cause — the honest reading is that the original failures are unexplained and are no longer occurring.

It now polls `/api/state` until both tickets carry the tag before reloading. Verified non-vacuous: asserting a tag name that does not exist gives `Received: 0`.

Assessment before building. The layout is more accommodating than it looks, but one architectural point decides the shape.

**The shell already has the right seam.** `App.tsx:1591` is a flex **row** (`flex: 1, overflow: hidden, position: relative`) holding `<main>` (the board) and the `<aside>`, and it already sits *below* the topbar and `TimeScrubber` inside a `height: 100vh` column. So "up to the beginning of the timeline layout" needs no measuring of the scrubber: that row's own height *is* the space between the timeline and the bottom of the window. Docking bottom is `flexDirection: 'column'` on that row, with the aside taking a `height` instead of a `width`, and the clamp falls out of the row.

**The one real constraint: dock side cannot live inside `Aside`.** The parent row's `flexDirection` depends on it, and `Aside` cannot style its own parent. So the preference has to be lifted into a small shared module (matching `usePersistedFlag`'s house pattern) that both `App` and `Aside` read — `epiq.aside.dock`, plus a separate `epiq.aside.height` since a bottom panel's size is not the width a side panel restores to.

**Everything else is small and already located:**
- Resize handle (`Aside.tsx:179-208`) is pinned `left: 0, top: 0, bottom: 0` with `ew-resize`. Bottom dock needs the mirror: `top` edge, full width, `ns-resize`, dragging `clientY`.
- The board spacer (`App.tsx:1740-1741`) keeps `scrollWidth` constant so the board does not bounce when the panel closes. A bottom panel takes vertical space, not horizontal, so the spacer is simply skipped while docked bottom — otherwise it reserves width for a panel that is not beside the board.
- `laneView` is `isFullscreen && panelWidth >= LANE_VIEW_WIDTH`. Docked bottom the panel is window-wide, so this becomes `(isFullscreen || dock === 'bottom') && …`. Worth *not* reducing it to width alone: `MAX_ASIDE_WIDTH` is 1400 and `LANE_VIEW_WIDTH` is 1400, so a side panel dragged to its maximum would otherwise flip into lanes on the last pixel.
- Fullscreen still overlays the row (`position: absolute; inset: 0`), so it keeps working from either dock.

**Scope note:** `Aside` also wraps the commit diff panel and the bulk panel, so the dock applies to all of them — which is right, but it means the switch is a panel-level preference, not a per-ticket one.

Open question for the user: how the side is switched — a button in the panel header, or dragging the panel to an edge. Asked in chat.

add.issue.comment.md:
Two corrections to the assessment above, after mapping the change surface properly.

**The height ceiling has to be measured, not calculated.** I said the board row's height is the budget, which is right, but `window.innerHeight − header − scrubber` would be the wrong way to get it: the scrubber is collapsible (`epiq.timeScrubber.collapsed`) and its height also varies with `layoutMode`, so the row's height changes without any window resize. The clamp reads the row's own `getBoundingClientRect()` instead.

**`board-gutter.pw.ts` will break, and could break silently.** It asserts `row.getBoundingClientRect().right === aside.getBoundingClientRect().left` — meaningless bottom-docked, where it becomes a top/bottom edge test. Worse, it locates the row as `main.lastElementChild`, so re-nesting `<main>` would make it pick a different element and pass vacuously. It gets updated as part of this, not after.

Also worth knowing before starting:
- `aside-stacking.pw.ts` asserts lanes are *absent* on a 1600px non-fullscreen panel. That holds only because the dock defaults to `right`; it is the test that would catch a default flipped by accident.
- `BulkDetails` renders `<Aside>` with no props at all — no fullscreen, no width tracking. Bottom-docked it becomes a wide, short strip of stacked sections. It will work, but it is the one panel that gains nothing from the dock.
- The spacer condition (`!commitDiff && !(selectedIssue && state?.user)`) does not exclude `BulkDetails`, so a multi-select with no selected issue currently renders both the panel and the spacer. Pre-existing, not introduced here, but adjacent enough to trip over.

Building the core now: dock preference, row flip, axis-generic panel and handle, lane view bottom-docked, header toggle, spacer skip, and the `board-gutter` update.

Solution: shipped in 3c2ece00 (PR #184, rebase-merged).

The panel docks to the bottom, spans the window, resizes vertically from its top edge, and shows the lanes without fullscreen — the three things the description asked for.

**Where the dock lives.** In `App`, not `Aside`: the row holding the board and the panel has to become `flexDirection: column`, and a component cannot style its own parent. `App` owns `epiq.aside.dock` and hands it down.

**Sizes are per side** — `epiq.aside.width` and `epiq.aside.height` are separate keys, so switching sides and back gives you the size you had there.

**The ceiling is measured.** The drag reads the board row's own `getBoundingClientRect()` at pointer-down. Deriving it as `window.innerHeight − header − scrubber` would have gone stale the moment the scrubber was collapsed or `layoutMode` changed, neither of which fires a window resize.

**The board spacer became side-specific.** It keeps `scrollWidth − clientWidth` constant so the board does not bounce when the panel closes; a bottom panel takes height instead, so reserving width for it would have shoved the board the other way. Skipped while docked bottom.

**`laneView` takes the dock, not width alone.** `MAX_ASIDE_WIDTH` and `LANE_VIEW_WIDTH` are both 1400, so a width-only test would flip a side panel into lanes on the last pixel of its drag.

**UI, after two rounds of feedback:** first a single toggle, then two devtools-style buttons, then those buttons tucked into a kebab in the panel header. Both sides show at once with the current one lit in accent, so it says where the panel is without a click. Choosing closes the menu — which the first version did not, and my own test caught it: re-clicking the kebab toggled the still-open menu shut rather than reopening it. `KebabMenu` gained an optional `title` and render-prop `children`; the swimlane menu passes its old title explicitly and is otherwise untouched.

**On the tests I flagged earlier:** `board-gutter.pw.ts` did not need changing after all. It asserts `row.right === aside.left`, which stays true because the dock defaults to `right` and no existing test changes it. Same for `aside-stacking`'s "no lanes at 1600 non-fullscreen". So the default is doing real work in keeping those valid — worth remembering before anyone changes it.

`aside-dock.pw.ts` covers the seam rotating from `main.right === aside.left` to `main.bottom === aside.top` and back, lanes without fullscreen, persistence across a reload, and the vertical drag growing the panel upward rather than off-screen.

Not done, and still true: `BulkDetails` gets the dock but gains nothing from it — bottom-docked it is a wide, short strip of stacked sections. Solution: a clock button on every Log row checks the board out at that moment. PR #185, branch `worktree-5RYVN23-log-checkout`.

The board already time-travelled; what was missing was aiming it at a moment you can name instead of one you drag for. The button reuses the scrubber's path — `Resume` in the header is still the way back.

The cut: `checkoutStateAtEvent` resolves the event's **effective** time and checks out at `time + 1`.
- `+1` because `splitEventsAtTime` cuts exclusively. Landing *on* the event shows the state it replaced, so "Changed description" would read the previous draft rather than the one that row wrote. Same convention `:peek next` uses.
- Effective, not raw, because the Log row displays `ulidTimeMs(event.id)` while the split judges by the clamped time — a poisoned far-future id would otherwise check out the whole log. Resolving it server-side also keeps event-log semantics out of the client, so the button sends an event id, never a timestamp.

Consequence worth knowing: once parked, the Log is the log of that moment too, so rows after the one you picked disappear until you resume.

Tests: unit cover the cut and the failure paths (verified red without the `+1`); schema covers the new message; `issue-history.pw.ts` drives the whole path — two description edits, check out the older, read the replaced draft, resume, read the current one. 981 unit + 82 GUI pass.
